text:
**Yes, a 20,000 mAh power bank is allowed on a flight, as long as you carry it in your cabin bag and not in checked luggage.**

**Why it qualifies**
- The FAA limits spare lithium-ion batteries and power banks to 100 Wh each. To convert, divide mAh by 1,000 and multiply by the voltage. Most power banks are rated at about 3.7 V, so 20,000 mAh works out to about 74 Wh, well under the limit. ([FAA: Airline Passengers and Batteries](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/airline-passengers-and-batteries))
- Power banks are carry-on only. If your carry-on gets gate-checked, take the power bank out and keep it with you in the cabin. ([FAA: Lithium Batteries](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/more_info/?hazmat=7))
- Protect the terminals from short circuits by keeping the bank in its retail packaging, a pouch, or a case, or by taping the terminals. ([FAA: Lithium Batteries](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/more_info/?hazmat=7))

**Things to check**
- Check the Wh rating printed on your bank. Some 20,000 mAh models use different cell voltages, but nearly all land under 100 Wh.
- Airlines can set stricter rules, such as a cap on how many power banks you can carry. The FAA says to check with your carrier before traveling. ([FAA](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/airline-passengers-and-batteries))
- Don't bring a damaged, swollen, or recalled battery. ([FAA: PackSafe](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe?packsafeq=power+bank))
- Banks over 100 Wh need airline approval, and anything over 160 Wh is not allowed. ([FAA](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/more_info/?hazmat=7))

**If you're shopping for one:** The [Baseus Blade H1 (20,000 mAh, 100 W)](https://dealectric.com/go/baseus-blade-h1-100w-20000mah) is listed at about 74 Wh and $89.99, so it fits under the carry-on limit. That Wh figure and price come from the retailer-affiliated page [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/answers/tsa-power-banks-spare-lithium-batteries-carry-on-only-2026-faa-100-wh), not the FAA, and that link is an affiliate link. It pays Dealectric if you buy, at no cost to you. Confirm the Wh rating on the product label before you fly.
